explanation: The thumbs-up was historically viewed as a rude, almost obscene gesture in parts of the Arab world, but decades of Western media exposure have made it widely understood as simply positive to many Saudis today. When then-candidate Donald Trump gave a thumbs-up during a 2017 visit to Saudi Arabia, commentary on whether it was offensive came mostly from Western observers rather than Saudis themselves, which illustrates how contested and generation-dependent the gesture's reception really is.
local_tip: With elders or in formal and religious settings, use a verbal acknowledgment rather than a thumbs-up to be safe.

also_check.note: The thumbs-up is still widely treated as an obscene insult there.
It's understood as 'good' or 'OK' and used positively, especially among younger people.
An abrupt or thrusting thumbs-up can be read as rude rather than complimentary by some.

sources.title: Trump Made A 'Rude' Thumbs Up Sign In Saudi Arabia — But Really Everyone Needs To Calm Down
